title: VPC Flow Log Analysis

controlTest.positiveScenario: Replay sample `aws:cloudwatchlogs:vpcflow` events with `action="REJECT"` into `index=aws`. Confirm UC-4.1.9 returns >=1 row and the alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign `aws:cloudwatchlogs:vpcflow` traffic without `action="REJECT"`. Confirm UC-4.1.9 returns zero rows and the alert does not fire.

dataSources: `index=aws` sourcetype=`aws:cloudwatchlogs:vpcflow` collected via `Splunk_TA_aws`; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
spl:
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudwatchlogs:vpcflow" action="REJECT"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.1.9_vpc_flow_log_analysis_9"
| sort -_time
description: UC-4.1.9 — VPC Flow Log Analysis: queries AWS `aws:cloudwatchlogs:vpcflow` for search criteria `action="REJECT"` and returns actor, resource, and region context for security review and change validation.
value: On AWS, 'VPC Flow Log Analysis' highlights abnormal network flow patterns—reconnaissance, lateral movement, or blocked exfiltration that perimeter tools may not correlate across cloud segments. UC-4.1.9 drives high-priority security alerting before customer-impacting drift.
implementation: Enable VPC Flow Logs on all VPCs (send to S3 or CloudWatch Logs). Ingest via Splunk_TA_aws. Create dashboards for rejected traffic, top talkers, and unusual port activity.
visualization: Table (top rejected flows), Sankey diagram (source to destination), Timechart, Map.
cimSpl:
| tstats `summariesonly` count
  from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
  where like(All_Traffic.action, "%eject%") OR like(lower(All_Traffic.action), "%deny%") OR like(lower(All_Traffic.action), "%block%")
  by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.dest All_Traffic.dest_port All_Traffic.action span=1h
| sort -count
dataModelAcceleration: Network_Traffic: requires VPC flow logs mapped to All_Traffic in CIM. Enable Data Model Acceleration for the CIM data models in `cimModels` once `Splunk_TA_aws` (and any CIM tags/aliases) map your fields; otherwise the `cimSpl` summary search may be empty. Step 2 on raw or metric indexes stays primary for most sites.
knownFalsePositives: Legitimate NACLs or security groups that block expected scanners; canary and migration traffic you already whitelisted in the runbook.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=aws`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_aws` with the modular input for `aws:cloudwatchlogs:vpcflow`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.1.78.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Enable VPC Flow Logs on all VPCs (send to S3 or CloudWatch Logs). Ingest via Splunk_TA_aws. Create dashboards for rejected traffic, top talkers, and unusual port activity.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudwatchlogs:vpcflow" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudwatchlogs:vpcflow" action="REJECT"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.1.9_vpc_flow_log_analysis_9"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `aws:cloudwatchlogs:vpcflow` in `index=aws` to detect vpc flow log analysis. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the provider cloud console audit view for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_1_9_alert` with severity aligned to `high` criticality. Dashboard: Table (top rejected flows), Sankey diagram (source to destination), Timechart, Map..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_aws` and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of vpc flow log analysis so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
